title: How to change cursor speed in Cursor on Mac: system settings guide for developers
metaTitle: How to change cursor speed in Cursor on Mac (System Settings)
description: Cursor does not have an internal setting to change cursor speed. Learn how to adjust your Mac system settings to control pointer speed for Cursor and everything else.
intro: There is no setting inside the Cursor editor to change your cursor speed because Cursor is a code editor, not a system-level application. To adjust the pointer speed, you must modify your macOS system settings, which will apply the change to Cursor and all other apps on your Mac.
tldr: Cursor does not include a specific setting for mouse or trackpad pointer speed.
Open the Apple menu and go to System Settings to change your global pointer speed.
If Cursor feels slow while coding, it is likely an issue with indexing or extensions, not your mouse speed.
Use the Command Palette to clear caches or restart the editor if you encounter lag.

blocks.text: Why Cursor lacks a cursor speed setting

Many users look for a way to change cursor speed in Cursor because they feel the pointer is moving too fast or too slow while they work. It is important to understand that Cursor is a text editor built on the VS Code framework. It does not control your hardware input devices. Your Mac manages the pointer speed through the operating system. When you change this setting in macOS, it affects every application you use, including your web browser, terminal, and code editor.
How to change cursor speed in macOS
Follow these steps to adjust your pointer speed for your entire system. These steps are for modern macOS versions.

items: Click the Apple Menu in the top left corner of your screen.
Find the Mouse or Trackpad section in the left sidebar.
Adjust the Tracking speed slider to your preferred level.
Test the movement immediately by moving your mouse across the screen.

blocks.text: Distinguishing between pointer speed and editor lag

If you find that Cursor feels laggy while you type or move the mouse, you might mistake this for a pointer speed issue. This is usually related to editor performance. Large codebases require significant system resources to index. If you have many extensions active, they can also consume CPU cycles and make the interface feel unresponsive.
When you feel like the editor is not keeping up with your input, try these steps to improve responsiveness.

items: Check your active extensions by pressing Cmd + Shift + X and disable those you do not need.
Reduce the number of files indexed by creating a .cursorignore file for large directories.
Switch to a lighter AI model in the Cursor Settings menu if the current one is causing latency.
Restart Cursor if the editor has been open for a long time to clear temporary memory usage.

blocks.text: Sometimes users feel their input is slow because their keyboard shortcuts are not triggering as expected. You can verify your shortcuts by using the command palette. Press Cmd + K followed by Cmd + S to open the keyboard shortcuts editor. Ensure that no custom settings are overriding your standard commands.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor speed only for Cursor?
faq.answer: No. Cursor does not have a setting for pointer speed. You must change the system-wide tracking speed in macOS settings.

faq.question: Why does Cursor feel slow when I move my mouse?
faq.answer: If the pointer itself feels slow, check your macOS system settings. If the editor interface feels laggy, check your CPU usage or reduce the number of active extensions.

faq.question: Does Cursor have a setting for the blinking text cursor?
faq.answer: The blinking text insertion point is a system-wide setting under Accessibility in macOS, not a setting within the Cursor application.

task: Change the global cursor speed on your Mac to improve your experience in Cursor.
appliesTo: All versions of Cursor on macOS.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner and select System Settings.

steps.name: Navigate to Mouse or Trackpad
steps.text: Find the Mouse or Trackpad option in the sidebar and click it.

steps.name: Adjust Tracking Speed
steps.text: Move the Tracking speed slider to the left or right to find your preferred speed.

troubleshooting.fix: Check for high CPU usage or try disabling unnecessary extensions.
Check for conflicting keybindings in the keyboard shortcuts menu.
